chunks: He made it such that there is no breaking of its bond, no loosening of its ring, no collapse of its foundation, no decay of its pillars, no uprooting of its tree, no ending of its duration, no expiry of its laws, no cutting of its branches, no narrowing of its paths, no difficulty in its ease, no darkness in its clarity, no crookedness in its straightness, no flaw in its wood, no obstruction in its vastness, no extinguishing of its lamps, and no bitterness in its sweetness.

key_terms.عُرْوَتِهِ: its bond/link (referring to the cohesive structure of religion)

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of Islam's permanence and perfection according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) employs a rich rhetorical structure of negation to affirm the eternal stability (thabat) and comprehensive perfection of Islam. This description aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding of the Quran and Sunnah as a complete, uncorrupted system where the 'roots' (usul) and 'branches' (furu') are equally enduring, reflecting the divine attribute of Al-Qayyum (The Self-Subsisting). The emphasis on clarity and ease underscores the accessibility of divine guidance, reinforcing the concept that the religion is free from the ambiguity or decay found in other systems.
